summary.prose: A changed file the index holds is brought up to date without a full reindex. A file that no longer exists is never stale. A file the index would never hold (an unsupported type, a lock file, a generated file or a path on the ignore list) is not stale. Any other stale changed file, whether it was never indexed or was indexed before a later edit the watcher missed, is queued once for indexing by the daemon's freshness handler, so a later poll of the gate finds it fresh. A file that cannot be indexed is never declared fresh: it stays stale until the existing freshness time-out sends the review to the degraded diff review. The review-session timeout seen on 2026-10-27 is a different defect handled elsewhere and is not part of this Story.

hldContextSlice.frameworkSummary: Standalone feature — no parent HLD. Design directly against the repo, grounded on the s1 analyze passes. There are no HLD shared contracts to honour.

migration.stateBefore: computeCodeReviewFreshness judges a changed file with entities by its watermark against its mtime, and a file with no entities by the repo-level lastIndexed against its mtime (bundle c1). lastIndexed is written when a full index completes and also at daemon start-up, right after the delta file jobs are enqueued and before they finish, so it cannot show that any one file is indexed (bundle c2). Nothing in the gate asks for indexing, and the codeReview.freshness handler is read-only (bundle c3). A deleted file has mtime 0 and is never stale today. A changed file the watcher missed, new or edited, or a file of a type the index never holds, stays stale until the next full reindex or a daemon restart.
migration.stateAfter: A changed file whose mtime is 0 is settled first and is never stale, as today. A file with entities keeps its watermark comparison. A file with no entities is classed by selectFile: a file the index would never hold is not stale; a selected file is stale. Every stale file the index holds, with an older watermark or without entities, is listed as unindexed, and the codeReview.freshness handler queues one file job for it per mtime and re-reads the queue, so a later poll finds it fresh. A file that is still stale after its request stays stale and is not requested again for the same mtime, so the existing freshness time-out sends the review to the degraded diff review. FreshnessResult has one more field, unindexedFiles. No stored data changes.

migrationSteps.action: Add the selection and requestedAt seams to FreshnessDeps and the unindexedFiles field to FreshnessResult, and the new rules to the compute with the mtime-0 case settled first and every stale held file listed, with the real selection seam in realFreshnessGraphDeps

In the codeReview.freshness handler, keep the in-memory request map, supply requestedAt from it, queue one file job for each file in unindexedFiles, record the time, and re-read the queue state for the reply

Update the existing whole-result assertions in freshness.test.ts, add the unit, integration and contract tests including the idle-queue missed-update case, and run the handler, routing, long-review, RPC fallback and review-stream-freshness tests unchanged
Restart the daemon so the running process uses the new handler; the request map starts empty, which only means each file is requested once more

migration.backwardCompat: The freshness IPC reply only gains unindexedFiles; clients that read isProcessing, inFlight, pendingCodeIndexJobs and staleFiles are unaffected. The controller-side wait loop, its freshness time-out and the diff-only fallback are unchanged. A client talking to an older daemon sees no unindexedFiles and the old behaviour.

alternativesConsidered.name: Classify with the index rule, and request indexing of every stale file the index holds
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Settle missing files first; class entity-less files with selectFile; and list every other stale file (entity-less and selected, or with an outdated watermark) so the daemon queues one file job for it per mtime.
alternativesConsidered.approach: A changed file with mtime 0 is settled first, as today. A file with entities keeps its watermark comparison and, when its watermark is behind its mtime, is stale and listed in a new unindexedFiles field. A file with no entities is classed by the existing selectFile rule through a new read-only selection seam: 'not-code' and 'excluded-by-ignore' files are not stale, and a 'selected' file is stale and listed. A listed file is left out of the list only when the daemon has already requested it at or after its mtime. The codeReview.freshness daemon handler queues one 'file' job for each listed file, records the request time, and re-samples the queue so the same reply shows isProcessing. A requested file that is still stale stays stale, so the controller-side wait ends through its existing freshness time-out in the degraded diff review.
pros: Fixes every way a held file stays stale: never indexed, or indexed and then edited with the watcher missing the update
A file the index will never hold stops counting as stale
Reuses selectFile and the existing file job; no new storage
A file the index cannot index is never declared fresh, so a failure still reaches the degraded diff review
cons: The freshness IPC gains a side effect (it queues work)
A file that cannot be indexed keeps the gate waiting until the freshness time-out (120 s by default) before the diff review

alternativesConsidered.name: Classification only
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Treat files the index would never hold as fresh; leave every other stale file stale.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Only the compute changes: it drops 'not-code' and 'excluded-by-ignore' files from staleFiles. Nothing is queued. A held file the watcher missed, new or edited, stays stale until a full reindex, a daemon restart or a later edit.
pros: Smallest change; the freshness IPC stays read-only
Removes the stale-forever case for unsupported file types, lock files and ignored paths
cons: Does not fix the observed case: the ten fixture files are code files the index would select
Does not fix a missed update of an indexed file
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Safe and small but leaves the observed case and the missed update unfixed; it violates the first fix criterion.

alternativesConsidered.name: Per-file index record
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: The indexer records, for every file event it handles, a per-file marker with the time and outcome, and freshness reads that marker.
alternativesConsidered.approach: The indexer writes a small record per file path with the time and outcome for the watcher path, the index.file path and the full index; freshness compares that record with the mtime.
pros: The decision is exact for every outcome, including failures
Independent of what entities a parser happens to produce
cons: New stored data and a write on every file event
Existing repositories have no records until a full index
Much larger than the defect needs
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Exact but a new stored record and a write on every file event for a defect that two small rules fix; partial on keeping existing behaviour and tests.

alternativesConsidered.name: Advance the repo watermark on incremental indexing
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Make each incremental file index move the repo-level lastIndexed.
alternativesConsidered.approach: After a 'file' job completes, the daemon sets the registered repo's lastIndexed to the time of the job.
pros: No change to the freshness compute
cons: Wrong meaning: lastIndexed would say the whole repo is current after one file
Does not help a file that was never indexed
Changes a value the repo status and the completeness report show
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Reports false freshness for unindexed files, so a mixed set reaches a full review without them; it violates the first and third fix criteria.

sequenceDefinition.narrative: How one poll of the freshness gate settles a missing file, finds the stale held files (never indexed, or with an outdated watermark), queues one index job for each and re-reads the queue so the same reply shows the work, and how a later poll finds the file fresh.
